input.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.
input.rationale: Section 16.2 imposes a blanket prohibition on assignment by either Party with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for IBM, and the "not unreasonably withheld or delayed" standard is granted only for MSL's assignments to MSL Related Companies — so IBM's assignments sit at the other Party's absolute discretion. That fails the fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice, consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld) and matches the walk-away description of a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. Section 5.1(b)(v) compounds this by giving each Party, including MSL, a termination right where substantially all of the other's shares or assets are acquired by a direct competitor — i.e. a Vendor exit right on IBM's change of control. Section 16.5 (MSL sale/merger notice and successor assumption) is favourable to us and untouched. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out plus a reasonableness standard in 16.2 and narrows 5.1(b)(v) to MSL-side acquisitions, preserving IBM's own termination right.

proposal.summary: Add IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out and reasonable-consent standard in 16.2; limit the competitor-acquisition termination trigger in 5.1(b)(v) so MSL cannot exit on an IBM change of control.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added our customary carve-out allowing IBM to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or asset sale (with notice), and made consent to other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard, since a blanket bar on IBM assignment with no M&A carve-out is not something we can accept. We also narrowed the competitor-acquisition termination trigger to MSL, as we cannot have MSL walking away on an IBM change of control; if helpful, we can instead discuss mutual successor-assignment rights on written notice.

ops.oldText: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party.
ops.newText: Except as expressly provided below, neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. IBM may, without MSL's consent and upon written notice to MSL, assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with IBM, or to any successor by way of merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of the assets of the IBM business to which this Agreement relates.

ops.oldText: v) substantially all of the shares or assets of one Party are acquired by an entity that competes directly with the other Party.
ops.newText: v) substantially all of the shares or assets of MSL are acquired by an entity that competes directly with IBM, in which case IBM may terminate.
